note: Covers the nine discourse chapters. Chapters 10-29 are collections of independent couplets and do not submit to a pericope schema at all; see structural_note. Chapters 30-31 (Agur, Lemuel, the acrostic) are discourse-shaped and can be indexed on this pattern, but are held until the couplet question is settled so the whole book is finished under one method rather than two.
structural_note: Proverbs 1-9 is continuous instruction — a father to a son, and Wisdom calling in the street — and indexes exactly like James or Jonah. Proverbs 10-29 is roughly 600 free-standing couplets in no narrative or argumentative order. Indexed at the density used for the first two books, that section alone would produce several hundred single-verse entries, most of them near-duplicates, and the index would become longer and less usable than the text it serves. That section needs a cluster entry — one entry gathering non-contiguous verses on a single theme — which the current schema cannot express, since it assumes one contiguous range per entry. That is a real decision about what the index is, not a formatting detail, and it is left open here deliberately.

entries.pericope: The purpose of the collection
entries.connection: The book states its own aim before saying anything else: not information but wise dealing, and prudence given to the simple. Wisdom is presented from the first line as a competence to be acquired, which is the premise C02 rests on.

entries.pericope: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge
entries.connection: The entrance requirement, already load-bearing in C02. Knowledge has a doorway and the doorway is a posture, which is why the road cannot begin with technique.

entries.pericope: If sinners entice you; the ambush that catches its own
entries.connection: The Two Ways given as a recruitment scene — one purse, one company, one road. The trap closes on the people who set it, which is C01's claim that the Way of Death is self-executing rather than externally punished.

entries.pericope: Wisdom cries in the street, and is refused
entries.connection: Wisdom is not hidden. She shouts at the city gates and is ignored, and the consequence is eating the fruit of one's own way. The first anchor for C06: the eyes are not opened by information becoming available, because it already was.

entries.pericope: Seek her as silver, search as for hidden treasure
entries.connection: A conditional with the effort placed entirely on the near side — receive, store, turn the ear, call out, seek, search — and understanding on the far side. Wisdom is given by God and searched out by the man, and the passage refuses to resolve that tension.

entries.pericope: Discretion will watch over you
entries.connection: Wisdom entering the heart is described as posting a guard — discretion watching, understanding keeping. Watchfulness presented not as vigilance the person supplies but as what interior wisdom does once it is there.

entries.pericope: Don't let kindness and truth forsake you
entries.connection: The pairing this entire road is named for. Hesed and emet are bound together at the neck and written on the tablet of the heart — held as one thing, worn where they can be seen, and inscribed where they cannot. The instruction is not to practice mercy and truth alternately but to refuse to let either leave.

entries.pericope: Trust with all your heart; don't lean on your own understanding
entries.connection: Already load-bearing in C02. The Discipline of Unknowing in its plainest form: not that understanding is worthless, but that leaning on it is the error. Verse 7 names the failure exactly — being wise in one's own eyes.

entries.pericope: Honor Yahweh with your substance and firstfruits
entries.connection: Giving from the first of the increase rather than from what remains after. Habitual Almsgiving grounded in sequence rather than in amount, which is what makes it a habit and not a response to surplus.

entries.pericope: Whom Yahweh loves, he reproves
entries.connection: Correction reframed as evidence of relationship rather than of rejection. Necessary before the Moral Audit can be survivable — a man who reads reproof as condemnation will not look in the mirror twice.

entries.pericope: She is a tree of life; by wisdom Yahweh founded the earth
entries.connection: Wisdom valued above silver, then immediately identified as the instrument of creation itself. The same faculty that orders a life ordered the world, which is the continuity the Landscape of Wonder depends on.

entries.pericope: Then you shall walk securely; your sleep will be sweet
entries.connection: The reward of kept wisdom described as unafraid sleep and a foot that does not stumble. The first anchor for C10 — remaining is not strain but the ease that follows it.

entries.pericope: Don't say to your neighbor, come again tomorrow
entries.connection: Good withheld when it is already in the power of the hand to give. Delay named as its own offense, which is what separates Spontaneous Service from generosity in principle. The first anchor for C13.

entries.pericope: He gives grace to the humble
entries.connection: The verse James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 both quote, in its original setting. Grace described as directed by posture, which is the whole architecture of the Hidden Life.

entries.pericope: Get wisdom, though it costs all your possessions
entries.connection: Instruction handed down a third generation — the father teaching what his own father taught him. Wisdom presented as inherited and as purchased, and the price named as everything.

entries.pericope: The path of the righteous is like the dawning light
entries.connection: Already load-bearing in C25. Growth described as increasing illumination rather than as arrival, and the contrast is not darkness that hurts but darkness that hides what one is stumbling over.

entries.pericope: Keep your heart with all diligence
entries.connection: The central text of C20 and the most cited verse of this book in the curriculum. The heart is guarded because it is the source, and what follows — the mouth, the eyes, the feet — is ordered outward from it in exactly that sequence.

entries.pericope: Her lips drip honey; the bitterness at the end
entries.connection: A trajectory traced from the sweetness at the start to the groaning at the latter end, with the regret given in the man's own voice. Interior Diagnosis run forward instead of backward: the beginning is judged by where it arrives.

entries.pericope: Drink water from your own cistern
entries.connection: Fidelity argued positively — satisfaction located in what one already has rather than restraint imposed on what one wants. The first anchor for C14, and the reason the household is treated there as a good rather than a limit.

entries.pericope: If you have become collateral for your neighbor
entries.connection: Urgent extrication from an obligation entered carelessly, with humbling oneself named as the means. Notable for treating a financial entanglement as a spiritual emergency, which is the stewardship logic the curriculum applies to money elsewhere.

entries.pericope: Go to the ant, you sluggard
entries.connection: The ant works without chief, overseer, or ruler, and the poverty arrives by increments of a little slumber. The Sacrifice of Routine grounded in unsupervised faithfulness, which is precisely what C13 means by ordinary.

entries.pericope: Seven things which are an abomination
entries.connection: A vice list running from haughty eyes to sowing discord among brothers, with the last given the emphatic position. The catalogue form C01 shares with the Didache's Way of Death, and the placement of discord last is not incidental.

entries.pericope: The commandment is a lamp; can a man scoop fire into his lap?
entries.connection: Teaching that walks with a man, watches while he sleeps, and speaks when he wakes — Watchfulness described as continuous rather than episodic. The fire and the coals then make the argument physical: some consequences are structural, not imposed.

entries.pericope: The young man void of understanding, watched from the window
entries.connection: The one extended narrative in this section, and the fall is located early — at the corner, in the twilight, before anyone speaks to him. The failure is a route taken, not a decision made, which is why C20 posts the watchman upstream of the moment of choice.

entries.pericope: Wisdom calls where the paths meet
entries.connection: Wisdom stationed at crossroads and city gates rather than in a sanctuary, claiming plainness as her own credential. Her words are said to be clear to whoever understands, which is the fruit test of C08 applied to speech before it is applied to teachers.

entries.pericope: I was the craftsman by his side, rejoicing before him
entries.connection: Wisdom present at the founding of the world and delighting in it daily. The strongest cosmological anchor in the Hebrew Scriptures for C24: the order a person is being formed into is the same order the world was made by.

entries.pericope: Watching daily at my gates
entries.connection: Blessing attached to daily waiting at the door rather than to a single act of finding. The Daily Anchors argued from the side of desire — the man is stationed there because he wants to be.

entries.pericope: Wisdom has built her house and set her table
entries.connection: Wisdom prepares a meal and sends her maidens to call in the simple by name. The invitation goes specifically to those who lack understanding, which sets the direction of the whole road: it is addressed to the unformed, not the qualified.

entries.pericope: Reprove a wise man and he will love you
entries.connection: Correction is triaged by the hearer rather than owed to everyone equally — reproving a mocker buys only insult. A restraint on rebuke that Covering Weakness needs, and one of the few places Scripture instructs a person to withhold a true word.

entries.pericope: Folly calls from her seat, using the same words
entries.connection: Folly sits at her door and calls the simple in language identical to Wisdom's, changing nothing but what is on the table. The counterfeit is deliberate and near-perfect, which is why C07 treats cleansed sight as prior to good judgment rather than as a product of it.
